claim_ceiling: Task-matched comparison plan for interaction-geometry inference, relational edge inference and closed-loop collective-motion prediction; not a composite life/intelligence detector
evaluation_principle: Baselines must be matched to the inferential task they actually solve. Do not compare one method's scalar accuracy with another method's rollout error, or treat predictive dependence as interventional causation.

baselines.citation: McKinney & Roy, A correlation based framework for inferring interaction geometry in collective motion, Scientific Reports (2026-08-17)
baselines.primary_task: Infer metric interaction radius and sensing angle from trajectory data.
baselines.reported_claim: 99.2% overall recovery accuracy on the paper's synthetic visual-Vicsek validation data; also tests topological Vicsek and empirical Golden Shiner trajectories.

data_source.licence: CC BY 4.0 stated on dataset page

baselines.limits: The 99.2% result is specific to synthetic visual-Vicsek geometry recovery, not causal discovery, general group intelligence, or life detection. Data package file inventory and per-file provenance still need admission.

baselines.citation: Han, Fink & Kammer, Collective relational inference for learning heterogeneous interactions, Nature Communications 15, 3191 (2024-04-12)
baselines.primary_task: Infer multiple interaction types jointly while accounting for correlations among incoming edges; Evolving-CRI updates edge posteriors for changing neighbourhood topology.
baselines.reported_claim: The paper reports improved heterogeneous interaction inference against independently inferred-edge baselines including NRI, and tests interpolation/extrapolation on an evolving-topology crystallization system. In that particle-system experiment, the interaction cutoff radius is assumed known.
baselines.limits: CRI addresses interaction-type inference and evolving topology, not by itself metric radius/sensing-angle estimation. The cited particle experiments assume the cutoff radius is known. Preserve that assumption in comparisons.

baselines.citation: Pan, Shi & Dokmanic, A Graph Dynamics Prior for Relational Inference, AAAI 38(13), 14508–14516 (2024)
baselines.primary_task: Infer direct interaction graphs from observed dynamics with a structural graph-dynamics prior; jointly fit shallow one-step and polynomial multi-step models.
baselines.reported_claim: The paper reports improved graph reconstruction and robustness to under-sampling versus earlier relational-inference methods on its evaluated tasks.

data_source.note: Recover exact datasets, generator versions, sampling rules and splits from the paper and public repository before reproducing.

baselines.limits: This is a direct interaction graph recovery comparator, not a metric-radius/sensing-angle benchmark or an intervention-based causal oracle.

baselines.citation: Liu, Li, Wang et al., Learning collective motion dynamics from trajectory data with physics-regularized graph neural networks, Complex & Intelligent Systems (published 2026-10-26)
baselines.primary_task: Predict long-horizon collective motion with dynamic focal-centred graphs, learned neighbour importance, physically motivated self-motion/alignment/spatial-interaction components, multi-step rollout loss and collective-behaviour regularization.
baselines.reported_claim: On six self-propelled-particle datasets, PR-GNN reports lower closed-loop position errors than all five evaluated baselines while preserving macroscopic indicators including polarization, rotational organization, mean speed and spatial spread.
baselines.licence: Article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Do not assume this grants rights to third-party data, code or adapted article material.
baselines.code_and_data_availability: The accessible main article page examined does not provide a code/data availability statement. Treat implementation and dataset access as pending; do not claim source reproduction.
baselines.limits: PR-GNN is a trajectory-prediction and collective-organization baseline. Its reported attention weights are post-hoc relational evidence, not by themselves causal edges or interventions.

matched_task_tracks.question: Can the system infer metric radius, field of view and sensing angle?
matched_task_tracks.rule: Reproduce the exact IGIC benchmark before extending to unseen parameter/seed regimes.

matched_task_tracks.question: Can the system infer correlated edge types and changing neighbourhood structure?
matched_task_tracks.rule: Keep the known-cutoff assumption explicit where the source experiment uses it.

matched_task_tracks.question: Can the system recover direct interactions when observation cadence hides immediate neighbours?
matched_task_tracks.rule: Match sampling rates, observation noise, system size and split protocol.

matched_task_tracks.question: Can the model preserve long-horizon individual trajectories and group-level organization?
matched_task_tracks.rule: Compare on the same six source datasets and exact rollout protocol when those materials become available.

matched_task_tracks.question: Does changing one agent's state alter another agent's subsequent behaviour?
matched_task_tracks.rule: Observational graph inference is not sufficient; require randomized/simulated intervention and matched sham controls.

oli_extensions: Cross-track calibration: geometry, edge type, rollout prediction and causal effect must retain separate outputs and uncertainty.
Topology mismatch: distinguish a calibrated effective interaction scale from an asserted physical radius when the true graph is topological.
Common-driver confounding: two agents responding to one exogenous process must not be assigned a direct causal edge without intervention evidence.
Nonreciprocity: infer directed influence when A affects B but B does not affect A.
Temporal aliasing: quantify how downsampling changes inferred neighbours, edge recovery and lag estimates.
Closed-loop mechanism challenge: compare forecast fidelity with recovery of the correct mechanism; a model may predict well with a wrong graph.
Model inadequacy: withhold qualification where the true generator is outside the candidate model family.

qualification_targets.note: Research targets only; none are current results.
qualification_targets.matched_source_reproduction: Reproduce each baseline's original metric on its own exact data/splits before declaring comparative improvement.
qualification_targets.closed_loop: On matched data, target at least 10% lower multi-horizon normalized rollout error than the strongest reproduced baseline, while not degrading registered macroscopic observables beyond their declared uncertainty.
qualification_targets.geometry: Maintain IGIC-level performance on the original synthetic visual-Vicsek test distribution, then improve selective risk and calibration on whole-seed/whole-regime holdouts.
qualification_targets.graph: At least 90% edge-direction recovery on held-out asymmetric known-truth systems at a preregistered sampling envelope.
qualification_targets.null_control: Zero false causal edges on at least 299 independent common-driver/no-coupling systems to target a one-sided 95% exact upper false-positive bound below 1%.
qualification_targets.adequacy: Zero false model-adequacy passes on the public omitted-mechanism negative controls.
qualification_targets.abstention: Report risk-coverage curves and prefer abstention over high-confidence geometry/edge claims under topology mismatch or inadequate cadence.

source_admission.IGIC: File inventory, exact seeds/splits, per-file hashes and rights must be verified.
source_admission.CRI: Verify GitLab source commit, ETH dataset file inventory and licences, and reproduce source splits.
source_admission.GDP: Pin GitHub commit, datasets and environment, then reproduce under-sampling cases.
source_admission.PR_GNN: Inspect supplementary PDF and contact authors for code/data where not stated; respect CC BY-NC-ND article licence and third-party data rights.
